lookedFor: robots.txt of openrouter.ai, read 2026-10-12 at 19:02 UTC: /sign-in is not disallowed.

The provider's Terms of Service, last updated 2026-08-31, section 7, Prohibited Conduct, item 5. Fragments as returned by the fetch tool: "develop, support or use software, devices, scripts, robots or any other means or processes", "(such as crawlers, browser plugins, add-ons or any other automated technology)", "to scrape or copy any information on the Site or the Services;".

The same section, item 6, fragment as returned by the fetch tool: "bypass any technical measures implemented by OpenRouter that are designed to prevent scraping;". Copying the form's structure is what a capture does, so on item 5 the page was not rendered and no capture exists.
This repository's preset table: the sign-in address only. No markup.

A web search for how sign-in works: the results quote third-party guides naming Google, GitHub, email and wallet sign-in. They do not say whether the email option takes a password or sends a code or link, and they do not name the identity provider.

KeePassXC-Browser's site list (commit 8b0b2c4) has no entry for this site. Chromium's public password-manager site tests (commit 88f1fe85) hold no recipes. Mozilla's published password recipes (13 records, read 2026-10-12) have no entry for this sign-in.
neededFromUser: First say how you sign in at https://openrouter.ai/sign-in: with a password, or with a code, a link or another account. If with a password: in your own browser, signed out, save the sign-in page, and the password page too if it is a separate one, before typing the password. Save each as Webpage, Complete (HTML only re-downloads the address and misses a scripted or submitted form). Keep the files outside the repository: they can hold your account name. Import: node scripts/capture-login-page.mjs --id openrouter --from-file <file.html>
